How to Write a Administrative Assistant Resume

An administrative assistant resume should show organization, judgment, confidentiality, and the volume of work coordinated. Replace broad support duties with the calendars, travel, records, and workflows you improved.

Example

Administrative Assistant resume summary

Use this as a pattern for level, scope, specialty, and evidence. Do not copy facts that are not yours.

Administrative assistant with 6 years of experience supporting multi-site leadership teams. Coordinated calendars across three time zones and introduced a travel workflow that reduced booking changes by 27%.
Recommended order

How to structure the resume

  1. Contact details and target title. Use the normal title from the job posting and provide working contact links.
  2. Focused summary. Establish your level, setting, specialty, and one representative outcome.
  3. Recent relevant experience. Use reverse chronological order and give the most space to work that resembles the target role.
  4. Role-specific skills. Keep a scannable list, then prove the important skills in bullets.
  5. Education and credentials. Training in office administration, bookkeeping, or sector systems can help. Experienced assistants should give more space to scope, discretion, and workflow improvements than to general coursework.
Use only what you can support

Skills to include

Match the employer's terminology when it accurately describes your experience.

  • Calendar management
  • Travel coordination
  • Meeting support
  • Document control
  • Office operations
  • Expense processing
  • Microsoft 365
  • Confidentiality
Evidence ideas

Useful metrics for a administrative assistant resume

Numbers should clarify scope or change. They do not need to be revenue figures.

Volume

Leaders, meetings, trips, or requests handled

Efficiency

Time saved or rework reduced

Accuracy

Records maintained or errors prevented

Writing patterns

Administrative Assistant resume bullet examples

Adapt the action, context, and result to your own verified work.

  • Coordinated complex calendars for four leaders across three time zones.
  • Introduced a travel workflow that reduced booking changes by 27%.
  • Organized board materials and maintained accurate confidential records.
  • Standardized purchase requests and cut approval follow-up by six hours per week.
Look for

Strong signals

  • Organization
  • Professional judgment
  • Service reliability
  • Confidentiality
Avoid

Common mistakes

  • Saying responsible for every routine task
  • Leaving the number of stakeholders unclear
  • Overemphasizing basic software knowledge
  • Using confidential details as proof

Questions, answered

Resume FAQ

What should a administrative assistant resume include?

Lead with organization, show relevant calendar management experience in context, and use achievement bullets that explain scope and outcome.

What skills belong on a administrative assistant resume?

Prioritize skills from the target job that you can prove in experience, projects, education, or credentials. Useful examples include calendar management, travel coordination, meeting support, document control.

Can I use the example numbers and bullet points?

No. The examples demonstrate structure and specificity. Replace every action, number, tool, and result with evidence that is true for your own work.

Which resume format should I use?

Reverse chronological format works for most candidates. Use a combination format when projects or transferable skills need more emphasis, but keep dates and work history clear.
